title: Implementation of Interference Reflection Microscopy for Label-free, High-speed Imaging of Microtubules
protocol: Insert a 50/50 mirror into the filter wheel of the fluorescent microscope using an appropriate filter cube.
Handle the 50/50 mirror with care as often they have anti-reflection coating.
Clean microscope slides and coverslips.
Modify the surface of the coverslips as needed, such as cleaning them using an alkaline detergent followed by 100% ethanol washes in between and after.
Cut 3 mm wide strips of plastic paraffin film using a razor blade.
Place two plastic paraffin film strips 3 mm apart on a clean cover slip to form a channel.
If using an upright microscope, place the strips on top of a clean microscope slide and then place a coverslip on top.
Place the coverslip (or slide) on a heat block at 100 °C for 10-30 seconds for the paraffin film to form a sealed channel.
Flow in 50 µg/mL of antibody (in Brinkley Buffer 80) by perfusion using a pipette.
Incubate for 10 min.
Wash five times with BRB80 buffer.
Flow in 1% poloxamer 407 (a triblock copolymer) in BRB80 to block the surface against non-specific binding.
Incubate for 10 min.
Wash five times with BRB80 buffer.
Place the sample on the microscope stage.
Turn on the epi-illumination light source.
Focus on the sample surface.
Find the sample surface by focusing on the paraffin film edge.
Set the field of view to the center of the chamber.
Center the field diaphragm in the field of view by closing it halfway and using the adjustment screws.
Reopen the diaphragm.
Slide in the Bertrand lens to view the exit pupil (back focal plane) of the objective.
Close the aperture diaphragm beyond the edges of the exit pupil of the objective.
Use the adjustment screws to center the aperture diaphragm with the exit pupil.
Open the aperture diaphragm and match its edges with those of the exit pupil.
Set the aperture diaphragm to about 2/3 of the NA of the objective.
Set the exposure time of the camera to 10 ms.
Adjust the illumination to nearly saturate the camera dynamic range.
Flow in 10 µL of GMPCCP- or taxol-stabilized microtubules in BRB80 by perfusion using a pipette.
Monitor binding by imaging the surface until 10-20 microtubules are bound within the field of view.
Wash the sample 2x with BRB80.
Set the microscope stage for microtubule visibility.
Acquire 10 images by setting a time lapse of 1 second delay between each image over 10 seconds with 10 ms exposure.
Move the stage along the channel long axis while acquiring 100 background images continuously at no delay and approximately 100 fps @ 10 ms exposure.
Calculate the median of the 100 background images to establish a reference background.
Set the sample heater temperature to 37 °C for microtubule dynamics imaging.
Flow in 10 µL of GMPCCP-stabilized microtubule seeds in BRB80 by perfusion using a pipette onto a fresh sample surface.
Monitor the binding of microtubule seeds to the surface live.
Wash the sample with 2x channel volume of prewarmed BRB80 at 37 °C or room temperature.
Flow in the polymerization mix containing 7.5 µM unlabeled tubulin, 1 mM GTP, and 1 mM DTT in BRB80 buffer.
Set up time-lapse acquisition using the microscope's software to take an image every 5 seconds for 15 minutes.
Acquire 10 images at each time point and average them to enhance contrast for measuring microtubule growth.
For microtubule shrinkage, set acquisition speed to 100 fps with a time delay of 0 and exposure time of 10 ms.
Acquire background image following the procedure in step 4.4.6.
Open saved background images using Fiji software.
Calculate median image (background) using Image > Stack > Z project > Median.
Open microtubule dynamics movie as a stack using File > Open.
Subtract background image from the microtubule dynamics stack using Process > Image calculator.
Draw a line along each microtubule of interest using the line tool and add to region of interest manager by pressing “t”.
Run the Multi-Kymo macro to generate a video and kymograph for every microtubule in the ROI manager.
Assign a unique identifier to each microtubule.
Run the Kymo-Analysis macro to measure growth rates and shrinkage rates of dynamic microtubules.
Prepare a sample of fluorescently labelled stabilized microtubules stuck to the surface.
Focus on the microtubules using the microscope focusing knob while imaging them with fluorescence.
Set camera exposure to 10 ms using the camera software.
Close down the aperture diaphragm (AD) to its smallest opening.
Adjust the illumination intensity to nearly saturate the camera’s dynamic range or to the maximum possible.
Acquire 10 images of a field of view containing at least 10 microtubules.
Acquire a background image.
Change the size of the AD and repeat imaging steps for the entire AD opening range from closed to exit pupil size.
Adjust illumination intensity each time the AD size is changed to match that of initial conditions.
Subtract the corresponding background image using an image calculator with "subtract" option.
Check the “32bit (float) result” option during subtraction.
Average the resulting images using a stack and Z project method.
Measure the signal-to-background noise ratio (SBR) of the microtubules.
Define SBR as the average intensity of the microtubule signal minus the intensity of the background, divided by the standard deviation of the background.
Calculate the average SBR of the microtubules for every opening size.
Set the AD size to the one producing the highest SBR.
Determine if there is a range of AD sizes that produce comparable contrast.
